title:  The Chi-Squared Test"
output: html_document

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

# Load your clean data
load(here("data/fw_nrc.rda"))
load(here("data/finn_clean.rda"))
```
### since I will try to give a mathematical andwer to the 2002 hypothesys i decided to go with a Chi-Squared test and put to test the idea that the trust and fear words were not upto chance. 
```{r}

# Count how many times the "master" is mentioned in each chapter
master_counts <- finn_clean |>
  filter(word == "master") |>
  count(chapter, name = "master_mentions")

# Find the median split to divide the book in half fairly
median_master <- median(master_counts$master_mentions, na.rm = TRUE)

### 2. Prep the Emotion Data 
chi_data <- fw_nrc |>
  # Focus strictly on the two emotions from the 2002 theory
  filter(sentiment %in% c("fear", "trust")) |>
  left_join(master_counts, by = "chapter") |>
  # If a chapter had no master mentions, set it to 0
  mutate(master_mentions = ifelse(is.na(master_mentions), 0, master_mentions)) |>
  # Categorize the environments
  mutate(Environment = ifelse(master_mentions >= median_master, 
                              "Master Present (Domestic)", 
                              "Master Absent (The Wild)"))

### 3. Build the Table and Run the Math
# Create the contingency table
sentiment_table <- table(chi_data$Environment, chi_data$sentiment)

# Print the raw table 
kable(sentiment_table, caption = "Word Counts: Environment vs. Emotion")

# Run the official test from stats package 
final_test <- chisq.test(sentiment_table)
print(final_test)
```
### with a p-value below .01 it is very likely that the hypothesis is correct and the shift in emotions were not an acciedent.
